sh_north_road.name: The North Road
sh_north_road.desc: A rutted track drops south off the Fallows' dikes onto open plough-land, hedge and furrow running out ahead under a wide, gray sky.
sh_north_road.brief: The rutted track down onto the plain.
onEnterOnce: This is the Shieldings: the open plain where the first Reeve's hired Companies broke a loyal shield-wall by dark, and both lines have held their ground, unrested, ever since.
Vell: "My own line's field, this — won here, the night the herald walked out with the white rod and was shot for his trouble. I have never once heard anyone in Marrowgate tell it that way."
Brother Osk: "Every hold has its grief, but I begin to think none of them has a priest who has buried nobody at all. I want to meet this one."
Tamsin: "The Free Companies were born on this ground, out of a broken truce and a captain's itchy trigger-finger. Worth remembering, whenever anyone tells you a hired sword answers to nobody."
Lys: "They say the crows never really left this field. I believe it. And I believe a dead herald is still owed the patience nobody gave him."

actions.label: guess which way the levy marched
fx: The ruts cut two ways, but only one is worn deep enough for men marching in step: south, into the Shieldings. None of them came back out on this road.

sh_west_road.name: The Drove-Road
sh_west_road.desc: A drove-road picks its way off the fen's last reed onto firm ground, cart-ruts deepening with every stride away from the standing water behind.
sh_west_road.brief: The drove-road, off the fen's last reed.
onEnterOnce: This is the Shieldings: the open plain where the first Reeve's hired Companies broke a loyal shield-wall by dark, and both lines have held their ground, unrested, ever since.

sh_green.name: Harrowfield — the Green
sh_green.desc: A worn green at the village's heart, a dry well at its center nobody has capped. Harrowfield's few streets run off it in every direction, and every one of them, sooner or later, leads back to the plain.
sh_green.brief: The green; every street leads back to the plain.

variants.desc: A worn green at the village's heart, a dry well at its center nobody has capped. The bread question is settled, one way or another, and nobody counts the loaves aloud anymore.
variants.brief: The green, its bread question settled.

variants.desc: A worn green at the village's heart, a dry well at its center nobody has capped. Since the truce was finally called, folk here talk of the field the way they'd talk of a debt finally paid, not a haunting.
variants.brief: The green; the old debt is paid now.

variants.desc: A worn green at the village's heart. Bread is watched closer than it used to be, since the best furlongs went to the dead for good — but nobody here will say the bargain was the wrong one.
variants.brief: The green; bread watched closer, since the bargain.

variants.desc: A worn green at the village's heart, a dry well at its center nobody has capped. Some evenings the wind off the plain still carries a smell that isn't quite woodsmoke, and nobody remarks on it twice.
variants.brief: The green; a smell on the wind some evenings.

sh_hearth.name: The Plough Hearth
sh_hearth.desc: Harrowfield's hearth-hall, low-beamed and always a little smoky, benches worn to the shape of generations of the same few families. A ladle and a cask of something rough sit ready by the fire for anyone who asks.
sh_hearth.brief: The hearth-hall, benches worn smooth by use.

actions.label: rest by the hearth
fx: You sleep to the tick of the fire and wake stiff but whole. Someone has already banked it fresh for the next stranger through the door.

sh_trade_counter.name: The Trade Counter
sh_trade_counter.desc: A plank counter under a sagging awning, rope and pitch and a few honest tools stacked behind it. Crake works it most days when he isn't out digging, weighing cinder-oil and old iron with the same flat scale.
sh_trade_counter.brief: A plank counter; rope, pitch, and dug iron.

actions.label: buy a length of dug-iron, honed (7 gold)
fx: Crake hones the edge once more before he'll hand it over. "Field-iron holds a better temper than you'd think. Everything out there's had four hundred years to season."

sh_reeve_yard.name: The Field-Reeve's Yard
sh_reeve_yard.desc: A working yard behind a low wall, ploughs racked and carts backed under a lean-to. A map of Harrowfield's furlongs hangs nailed to the post, one long strip near its center left carefully, permanently blank.
sh_reeve_yard.brief: A working yard; one furlong left blank on the map.

variants.desc: A working yard behind a low wall. The furlong map hangs as it always did, except now a second strip is inked out beside the first, and a third, wherever the ploughs had to give further ground.
variants.brief: The yard; more furlongs inked out now.

sh_stonecutter_lodge.name: The Stone-Cutter's Lodge
sh_stonecutter_lodge.desc: A mason's lodge, chisels racked by size, a half-dressed block of good gray stone standing under canvas at its center like something waiting to be told what it's for.
sh_stonecutter_lodge.brief: A mason's lodge; a half-dressed stone under canvas.

variants.desc: A mason's lodge, chisels racked by size. The canvas is gone from the block at its center, its face cut clean and bare, a Crown seal already blocked in above the first line.
variants.brief: The lodge; the stone cut for a Crown seal.

variants.desc: A mason's lodge, chisels racked by size. The block at its center bears a rough charter-mark now, cut plainer than Bevan is used to being asked for.
variants.brief: The lodge; the stone cut for a charter-mark.

variants.desc: A mason's lodge, chisels racked by size. The block at its center is covered in names, cut small and even, running edge to edge with no room left for anything grander.
variants.brief: The lodge; the stone cut small, edge to edge.

variants.desc: A mason's lodge, chisels racked by size. The block at its center carries a wording Bevan still isn't sure he likes, though he can't say which line he'd cut instead.
variants.brief: The lodge; a wording nobody quite loves.

variants.desc: A mason's lodge, chisels racked by size. The block at its center still stands under its canvas, and Bevan has stopped pretending he expects to uncover it.
variants.brief: The lodge; the stone still stands under canvas.

sh_pensioners_house.name: The Pensioner's House
sh_pensioners_house.desc: A snug house kept too tidy for a soldier's, a company banner's bare staff racked over the mantel and a roll of names under glass beside it, the ink gone brown but every letter still true.
sh_pensioners_house.brief: A tidy house; a bare banner-staff over the mantel.

variants.desc: A snug house kept too tidy for a soldier's. The Companies' first banner hangs on the staff over the mantel again, faded to the colour of old rope, beside the roll of names under glass; Ossett keeps looking up at it.
variants.brief: The house; the staff bears its cloth again.

sh_chantry_porch.name: The Field Chantry Porch
sh_chantry_porch.desc: A small chantry's porch, a rain-swollen door behind it and a chained ledger on a reading-stand, thick with names the porch keeps but the ground behind the door has never once received.
sh_chantry_porch.brief: The chantry porch; a chained ledger of names.

sh_remembrancers_cot.name: The Remembrancer's Cot
sh_remembrancers_cot.desc: A narrow cot stacked floor to rafter with tally-boards, each one a levy's name and the ditch he stood in, kept the way the Keepers keep a covenant: exactly, and without anyone thanking her for it.
sh_remembrancers_cot.brief: A narrow cot; tally-boards floor to rafter.

sh_ditch_gate.name: The Ditch-Gate
sh_ditch_gate.desc: Harrowfield's last gate, its timbers scarred where every plough and every funeral has passed for four hundred years. Beyond it, the ground stops being anyone's and starts being the plain's.
sh_ditch_gate.brief: The last gate; beyond it, the open plain.

sh_measuring_chain.name: a brass furlong-chain
sh_measuring_chain.hint: Sten counts every furlong with this; he'd notice it gone

sh_iron_blade.name: a length of dug-iron, honed
sh_iron_blade.hint: field-iron, four hundred years seasoned; a step above a belt-knife

sh_road_buckle.name: a corroded belt-buckle, army-issue
sh_road_buckle.hint: no belt left to hold; the strap rotted off it long ago

sh_road_tally.name: a drover's tally-stick, notched
sh_road_tally.hint: one notch short of a full count; whoever kept it never finished
